summary: Singapore's Global Investor Programme gives permanent residence (not citizenship) to business owners and investors; terms are traceable from 2005 through archived EDB/Contact Singapore factsheets, an EDB 2023 release and Hansard (S$1m-2m options until 2010, S$2.5m from 2011, S$10m/S$25m/S$200m-AUM family office from 15 Mar 2023, listed-equities rule from Feb 2025). Numbers come only as rounded multi-year totals in ministerial answers (1,826 PRs 2004-Jun 2017; ~200 in 2020-2022; ~450 in 2015-2025) plus investment, spending and jobs figures; no annual series exists. Official sources tie the 2023 S$3 billion money-laundering case to tax-incentivised family offices and to foreign CBI passports, not to the GIP.

observations.quote: As of June 2017, 1,826 GIP applicants have been granted permanent residency since the programme's inception in 2004.
observations.notes: GIP applicants (main applicants) granted PR from 2004 to June 2017. Whether dependants are excluded is not stated, but the count is of "applicants".

observations.quote: Of these, 67 have been granted citizenship.
observations.notes: GIP PR holders (of the 1,826) who later became Singapore citizens through the normal citizenship process; the GIP itself grants PR, not citizenship.

observations.quote: One GIP investor had his PR status revoked upon review.
observations.notes: PR revoked after review, of the 1,826 GIP PRs granted to June 2017.

observations.quote: Over the past three years, the GIP has attracted close to 1,000 investors who have invested over $1.5 billion either in an approved investment fund or directly in a business in Singapore.
observations.notes: 'Close to 1,000' investors over 'the past three years' as of 22 Nov 2010 (exact months not given). The question asked how many were granted PR; the answer says 'attracted', so this is read as investors admitted under the GIP. Recorded as an upper approximation.

observations.quote: Over the past three years, the GIP has attracted close to 1,000 investors who have invested over $1.5 billion either in an approved investment fund or directly in a business in Singapore.
observations.notes: 'Over $1.5 billion' (Singapore dollars; the answer uses $ for S$) invested in GIP funds or businesses by investors admitted over the three years to Nov 2010. Reported investment, not applications multiplied by the minimum.

observations.quote: Mr Speaker, about 200 individuals were accorded permanent residency through the Global Investor Programme (GIP) from the years 2020 to 2022.
observations.notes: Rounded figure ('about'/'around') given by the minister; recorded as estimate because no exact count was published. In a supplementary reply the minister called them 'about 200 GIP investors', i.e. main applicants. She also said GIP PRs are 'much lesser than 1%' of all PRs approved each year.

observations.quote: Between 2020 and 2022, an average of 60 investors were accorded Singapore Permanent Residence (PR) status through the GIP annually.
observations.notes: EDB's own figure; an annual average, consistent with 'about 200' over three years in sgp-parl-oa-gip-2023.

observations.quote: From 2015 to 2025, around 450 individuals were accorded permanent residency through the GIP.
observations.notes: Rounded figure ('about'/'around') given by the minister; recorded as estimate because no exact count was published. 'Individuals' is not defined; the 2023 answers used the same word for investors (main applicants).

observations.quote: The distribution across options (a), (b) and (c) is approximately 50%, 40% and 10% respectively.
observations.notes: Share of the ~450 GIP PR grants 2015-2025 under Option A (business investment).

observations.quote: The distribution across options (a), (b) and (c) is approximately 50%, 40% and 10% respectively.
observations.notes: Share of the ~450 GIP PR grants 2015-2025 under Option B (GIP fund / GIP-select fund).

observations.quote: The distribution across options (a), (b) and (c) is approximately 50%, 40% and 10% respectively.
observations.notes: Share of the ~450 GIP PR grants 2015-2025 under Option C (single family office). Option C only existed from March 2020.

observations.location: written answer, para beginning "To Ms Mariam's interest on the GIP"
observations.quote: Since 2020, a small number of about 30 SFO owners have been supported under the GIP
observations.notes: Single family office (SFO) owners 'supported under the GIP' from 2020 to the date of the answer (6 Jul 2023). 'Supported' is read as accorded PR under the family-office route; the answer does not say so in those words.

observations.quote: Over the same period, about $500 million was invested directly in new or existing Singapore-based business entities.
observations.notes: Direct investment (Option A route) by GIP PRs granted 2015-2025. Singapore dollars.

observations.quote: Another $430 million was placed in GIP funds that invest in Singapore-based companies.
observations.notes: Money placed in GIP funds (Option B) by GIP PRs granted 2015-2025. Singapore dollars. The minister added that Option B applicants choosing the new GIP-select funds had not yet confirmed their investments.

observations.location: supplementary reply to Mr Yip Hon Weng
observations.quote: As of October 2022, GIP investors have also injected S$1.62 billion into approved GIP funds.
observations.notes: Cumulative money injected into approved GIP funds (Option B) as of Oct 2022; start date not stated. Of this, S$1.41 billion (87.2%) had been deployed and S$930 million invested in Singapore-based companies.

observations.location: supplementary reply to Mr Thomas Chua
observations.quote: I can share that, as of 2017, the total GIP funds amount to $1.5 billion
observations.notes: 'Total GIP funds' as of 2017, Singapore dollars. Unclear whether this is money committed by GIP investors or the funds' total size.

observations.quote: From 2011 to 2016, GIP investors brought in $1.8 billion in total business expenditure via direct investments, generating over 6,000 job opportunities in Singapore.
observations.notes: Total business expenditure by companies of GIP investors who invested directly (not fund investors). Singapore dollars.

observations.location: supplementary reply to Mr Yip Hon Weng
observations.quote: The GIP investors brought in more than S$5.46 billion in total business expenditure via direct investments.
observations.notes: 'More than S$5.46 billion', 2011-2022 ('over an 11-year period' per the minister). Direct-investment route only.

observations.location: Minister for Trade and Industry, GIP passage
observations.quote: Over the past 11 years, GIP investors have brought in around $5.5 billion in total business expenditure, generating over 24,000 jobs in Singapore.
observations.notes: 'Past 11 years' as of Feb 2023; probably the same 2011-2022 figure as sgp-parl-oa-gip-2023 (S$5.46 billion) rounded. Period label is approximate.

observations.quote: Between 2011 and 2022, GIP investors created 24,699 jobs across a range of roles
observations.notes: Jobs created by GIP investors (all nationalities of employees unless stated; not limited to Singaporeans).

observations.location: supplementary reply to Mr Yip Hon Weng
observations.quote: This is generating more than 24,000 jobs in Singapore.
observations.notes: 'More than 24,000' jobs from direct investments 2011-2022; EDB's exact figure is 24,699 (sgp-edb-gip-mr-2023).

observations.quote: From 2011 to 2016, GIP investors brought in $1.8 billion in total business expenditure via direct investments, generating over 6,000 job opportunities in Singapore.
observations.notes: 'Over 6,000 job opportunities'.

observations.quote: Close to 100 have invested directly in businesses ranging from engineering, R&D, shipping, asset management and services and trading, creating some 1,500 jobs.
observations.notes: 'Some 1,500 jobs' from close to 100 investors who invested directly in businesses, over the three years to Nov 2010.

observations.quote: Close to 100 have invested directly in businesses ranging from engineering, R&D, shipping, asset management and services and trading, creating some 1,500 jobs.
observations.notes: Of the 'close to 1,000' GIP investors over the three years to Nov 2010, 'close to 100' invested directly in businesses (the rest in approved funds).

observations.quote: From 2016 to 2025, around 85% of the individuals accorded permanent residency through the GIP remained a PR as of 31 December 2025.
observations.notes: Share of people granted GIP PR in 2016-2025 who were still PRs on 31 Dec 2025 (those who became citizens presumably count as no longer PR; not stated).

observations.quote: Fewer than 25 individuals did not have their re-entry permits renewed as they did not meet the prevailing criteria, such as economic contribution and length of residency.
observations.notes: UPPER BOUND, not a count: the source says 'fewer than 25'. GIP PRs (granted 2016-2025) whose re-entry permits were not renewed; without a valid re-entry permit the PR status lapses once the person leaves Singapore. The source says only fewer/less than 25; recorded as a range from 0 to 25 (upper bound).

observations.quote: Fewer than 20 individuals were granted Singapore citizenship.
observations.notes: UPPER BOUND, not a count: the source says 'fewer than 20'. GIP PRs (granted 2016-2025) who later obtained citizenship. The source says only fewer/less than 20; recorded as a range from 0 to 20 (upper bound).

observations.quote: From 2004 to 2012, a total of 1,080 investors were granted permanent residence (PR) status under the Financial Investor Scheme (FIS).
observations.notes: Investors granted PR under the Financial Investor Scheme, a separate investor-PR scheme that ended on 15 Apr 2012.

observations.quote: In the same period, 194 applications were rejected.
observations.notes: Financial Investor Scheme applications rejected 2004-2012.

observations.quote: As of 31 December 2023, there were around 1,400 Single Family Offices (SFOs) that have been awarded tax incentives
observations.notes: MAS tax incentives under sections 13O/13U of the Income Tax Act. These incentives do not confer residence; listed because GIP Option C requires a single family office. Not the number of GIP family-office PRs.

observations.quote: As of end-December 2025, more than 2,000 Single Family Offices (SFOs) receive tax incentives
observations.notes: 'More than 2,000'. MAS 13O/13U tax incentives; not a residence programme. See sgp-parl-wa-sfo-2024 for end-2023.

program_terms.quote: Under a new option to the current GIP, a foreigner can now be considered for PR status if he invests at least $2 million in business set-ups, other investment vehicles such as venture capital funds, foundations or
program_terms.notes: S$2 million in businesses, funds, foundations or trusts and/or private homes, with at most half in residential property ('This policy change will take immediate effect'). Later listed as Option C (sgp-cs-gip-factsheet-2009). valid_to: the property option was dropped from 1 Jan 2011 (sgp-cs-gip-factsheet-2010).

program_terms.quote: Option A: Invest at least S$1 million in a new business startup or expansion of an existing business operation.
program_terms.notes: Start date not found: the factsheet is undated (PDF created June 2009) and only shows these terms were in force in 2009-2010. Option A. Replaced by S$2.5 million from 1 Jan 2011.

program_terms.quote: Option B: Invest at least S$1.5 million in a new business startup, expansion of an existing operation, or a GIP-approved fund
program_terms.notes: Start date not found: the factsheet is undated (PDF created June 2009) and only shows these terms were in force in 2009-2010. Option B: business or GIP-approved fund.

program_terms.quote: Option C: Invest at least S$2 million 2 in a new business startup, expansion of an existing operation, or a GIP-approved- fund.
program_terms.notes: Start date not found: the factsheet is undated (PDF created June 2009) and only shows these terms were in force in 2009-2010. Option C. Footnote 2: 'Up to 50% of the investment amount can be invested in residential property, for owner occupancy only.' The same option is in the Oct 2010 factsheet (sgp-cs-gip-factsheet-2010).

program_terms.quote: Your parents and parents-in-law are eligible for PR at an additional investment of S$300,000 per person under your application.
program_terms.notes: Start date not found: the factsheet is undated (PDF created June 2009) and only shows these terms were in force in 2009-2010. Additional investment per parent included for PR. From 1 Jan 2011 parents could no longer be included (only a Long Term Visit Pass).

program_terms.quote: Option A: Invest at least S$2.5 million in a new business entity or expansion of an existing business operation.
program_terms.notes: Announced in the Oct 2010 factsheet as taking effect 'from 1 January 2011'; confirmed by sgp-parl-wa-gip-2010 and sgp-cs-gip-factsheet-2011. Unchanged in 2012, 2014 and 2021 factsheets. From 2012 the factsheet required a 3-year (later 5-year) business plan; renewal later required 10 employees (5 citizens) and S$2 million annual business spending (sgp-edb-gip-mr-2023 annex). valid_to: replaced 15 Mar 2023.

program_terms.quote: Option B: Invest at least S$2.5 million in a GIP-approved fund.
program_terms.notes: From 1 Jan 2011. By Oct 2012 the fund had to be 'a GIP fund that invests in Singapore-based companies' (sgp-cs-gip-factsheet-2012); in 2023 EDB described the old rule as a fund investing at least 50% in Singapore-based companies (sgp-edb-gip-mr-2023 annex). Replaced 15 Mar 2023.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant; single family office with AUM of at least S$200 million
program_terms.quote: Option C: Invest S$2.5 million in a new or existing Singapore-based single family office having Assets-Under-Management (AUM*) of at least S$200 million.
program_terms.notes: Introduced in the March 2020 revision (date from sgp-edb-gip-mr-2023 para 11; no 2020 document found). Footnote: offshore assets count toward the AUM if at least S$50 million is transferred into and held in Singapore. Only for applicants with at least S$200 million in net investible assets (Family Office Principals) or the other profiles.

program_terms.quote: Demonstrate an investment of at least S$10 million, inclusive of existing paid-up capital, in a new business entity or existing business operation in Singapore
program_terms.notes: Option A from 15 Mar 2023. Re-entry permit renewal after 5 years needs at least 30 employees, half of them citizens and 10 new hires. Still current in the May 2025 factsheet (sgp-edb-gip-factsheet-2025, p. 4) and the Feb 2026 parliamentary answer.

program_terms.quote: Under Option B, applicants will be required to invest S$25 million in a GIP-select fund.
program_terms.notes: Option B from 15 Mar 2023; seven GIP-select funds were appointed on 1 Jun 2023 (sgp-edb-gipselect-mr-2023, which calls it 'a tenfold increase from the required amount of S$2.5 million'). Investment must be maintained for re-entry permit renewal.

program_terms.applies_to: single family office assets under management (may be partly offshore)
program_terms.quote: Under Option C, applicants will be required to establish a Singapore-based Single- Family Office (SFO) with Assets-Under-Management (AUM) of at least S$200 million, of which at least S$50 million must be deployed and maintained in any of the following four investment categories
program_terms.notes: Option C from 15 Mar 2023: total AUM requirement. See the family_office_deployed rows for the part that must be in Singapore.

program_terms.applies_to: amount transferred into Singapore and deployed in qualifying investments
program_terms.quote: of which at least S$50 million must be deployed and maintained in any of the following four investment categories
program_terms.notes: Four categories: MAS-licensed exchange listings (incl. REITs and business trusts per sgp-edb-gip-factsheet-2023), qualifying debt securities, funds of Singapore-licensed managers, private equity in non-listed Singapore businesses. Deploy within 12 months of final approval and maintain for the 5-year re-entry permit. Narrowed from 21 Feb 2025.

program_terms.applies_to: amount that must be deployed in equities listed on approved Singapore exchanges

The May 2025 factsheet lists only 'Equities listed on Singapore approved exchanges' (sgp-edb-gip-factsheet-2025, p. 4). Does not affect MAS tax-incentive criteria.

program_terms.notes: Non-refundable EDB application fee in the 2 Oct 2012 factsheet. Dates of introduction and change not found; the 2009-2011 factsheets mention no fee.

program_terms.notes: Fee in the factsheet version of March 2014 (captured 2015). Exact start date not found.

events.title: Private residential property removed from GIP investments
events.description: According to a 2005 ministerial statement, private homes had been allowed as a GIP investment but were removed from the list of allowable instruments in 1996. This implies an investor-PR scheme under the GIP name before the 2004 date MTI gives as the programme's inception.
events.quote: Private residential properties, which had been allowed under the GIP, were removed from the list of allowable investment instruments under the scheme in 1996.

events.title: Global Investor Programme starts (per MTI)
events.description: MTI and EDB give 2004 as the start of the GIP (run by Contact Singapore, part of EDB). The 2005 statement shows a scheme of that name existed earlier; 2004 may mark a relaunch. Not resolved.

events.title: Private homes re-allowed: S$2 million option with up to 50% in residential property
events.description: Minister for National Development announced a new GIP option: invest at least S$2 million in businesses, funds, foundations or trusts and/or private residential property, with up to half in property, with immediate effect.
events.quote: This policy change will take immediate effect.

events.title: Minimum investment raised to S$2.5 million; property option and parents dropped
events.description: From 1 Jan 2011 the options became S$2.5 million in a business (A) or a GIP-approved fund (B); partial investment in residential property ended, and parents could no longer be included for PR.
events.quote: Please note that the following changes in investment options will take effect from 1 January 2011

events.title: Financial Investor Scheme ends
events.description: The Financial Investor Scheme, a separate investor-PR route (1,080 investors granted PR 2004-2012), ceased.
events.quote: The FIS has ceased with effect from 15 April 2012.

events.title: Government says GIP assessment criteria were recently reviewed and tightened
events.description: Asked about foreigners involved in embezzlement, the Minister of State said the criteria had been reviewed and tightened (notarised documents, bank references, declarations of criminal convictions, screening by other agencies). The Oct 2012 factsheet shows higher turnover thresholds (S$50 million; S$200 million for real estate and construction firms) and requires Option B funds to invest in Singapore-based companies. Exact date of the change not found.
events.quote: The assessment criteria for applicants under the Global Investor Programme (GIP) was reviewed and tightened recently.

events.title: GIP revised: new applicant profiles and a family-office option (Option C)
events.description: EDB revised the GIP to cover next-generation business owners, founders of fast-growing tech companies and family office principals; a new Option C allowed investing S$2.5 million in a Singapore single family office with at least S$200 million in AUM (terms in sgp-edb-gip-factsheet-2021).
events.quote: The GIP was last revised in March 2020, when changes were made to address the emergence of new breeds of business owners, including founders of fast-growing tech companies and family office principals.

events.title: Minister announces higher GIP investment quantum
events.description: In the Committee of Supply debate the Minister for Trade and Industry said EDB would raise the GIP investment quantum and adjust GIP-select funds.
events.quote: the Economic Development Board will enhance the GIP by raising the investment quantum

events.title: Thresholds raised: S$10 million (business), S$25 million (GIP-select fund), family office must deploy S$50 million
events.description: Changes announced by EDB on 2 Mar 2023 and effective 15 Mar 2023: Option A from S$2.5 million to at least S$10 million with 30 employees for renewal; Option B from S$2.5 million to S$25 million in a GIP-select fund; Option C requires an SFO with AUM of at least S$200 million of which S$50 million deployed in four Singapore investment categories.
events.quote: The changes will take effect from 15 March 2023.

events.title: EDB appoints seven GIP-select funds
events.description: EDB named seven fund managers (B Capital, East Ventures, GGV, HHLR, Insignia, Jungle Ventures, Vertex) as GIP-select funds for Option B.
events.quote: The Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) has appointed seven fund management companies as Global Investor Programme (GIP)-select funds.

events.title: Money-laundering raids: ten foreign nationals arrested, several holding passports of citizenship-by-investment countries
events.description: Police raids on 15 Aug 2023 led to ten arrests in what became the S$3 billion case. The police release lists, among the passports held: Cyprus (two arrested were Cypriot nationals), Vanuatu (one Ni-Vanuatu national; Vanuatu passports also held by two others), St Kitts and Nevis, Turkey, Cambodia, and what the release calls the "Dominican Republic". This links the case to foreign citizenship-by-investment programmes; the official sources found do NOT link any of the accused to Singapore's GIP (see the 3 Oct 2023 statement: the ten held Employment Passes and Dependant's Passes).
events.quote: The man was also found in possession of a foreign passport believed to be issued by St Kitts and Nevis and the woman was found with other foreign passports believed to be issued by the Dominican Republic and Turkey.

events.title: Ministerial statement: accused held work and dependant passes; some linked to tax-incentivised family offices
events.description: Second Minister for Home Affairs: the ten arrested hold Employment Passes and Dependant's Passes; assets seized or frozen exceed S$2.8 billion. Minister of State Alvin Tan (for MAS): one or more accused may have been linked to single family offices awarded tax incentives. No mention of the GIP.
events.quote: They hold Employment Passes and Dependant's Passes.

events.title: Six tax-incentivised family-office funds linked to convicted persons; tax benefits withdrawn
events.description: Six single family office funds that received MAS tax incentives were linked to people convicted in the money-laundering case or their spouses; benefits withdrawn from the year of charge or conviction, earlier benefits not clawed back.
events.quote: A total of six single family office (SFO) funds which were awarded SFO tax incentives have been identified to be linked to individuals who have been convicted in relation to the money laundering case or their spouses.

events.title: Family-office option: S$50 million must go into Singapore-listed equities
events.description: New GIP Option C applicants must deploy at least S$50 million in equities listed on approved Singapore exchanges (REITs and bonds no longer count), a measure of the Equities Market Review Group.
events.quote: From 21 February 2025, new GIP applicants under this option

events.title: S$2.79 billion in assets surrendered to the state in the S$3 billion case
events.description: As of December 2024, about S$2.79 billion of assets linked to the case had been surrendered to the state (S$1.54 billion in cash or financial assets).
events.quote: As of December 2024, assets amounting to approximately $2.79 billion, linked to the $3 billion money laundering case, had been surrendered to the state.

events.title: Two tax-incentivised family-office funds linked to sanctioned Prince Group individuals
events.description: MAS identified two SFO funds with tax incentives linked to individuals sanctioned by the US (Chen Zhi and associates) and ceased the incentives. About 3% of 1,300 SFO tax-incentive applications over three years were rejected. Not linked to the GIP in the answer.
events.quote: Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has identified two Single Family Offices (SFO) funds granted tax incentives that are linked to the sanctioned individuals.

programs.name: Global Investor Programme (GIP)
programs.notes: Permanent residence (not citizenship) for business owners and investors, run by Contact Singapore, a division of the Economic Development Board (EDB); approvals issued by the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority. No law establishing the scheme was found; it is run administratively. MTI dates it to 2004, though a 2005 ministerial statement refers to GIP rules changed in 1996. Applicants must first meet business track-record tests (e.g. company turnover of S$200m now) or, for family-office principals, S$200m in net investible assets; then invest under Option A (business, S$10m since 15 Mar 2023), B (GIP-select fund, S$25m) or C (single family office, AUM S$200m with S$50m deployed in Singapore, since Feb 2025 in listed equities). PR comes with a 5-year re-entry permit renewed only if business, jobs and residence conditions are met. Citizenship is not part of the scheme: GIP PRs may apply for it through the normal process (67 of 1,826 had by June 2017). Separate from the MAS 13O/13U family-office tax incentives, which give no residence rights.

programs.name: Financial Investor Scheme (FIS)
programs.notes: Separate investor permanent-residence scheme. 1,080 investors granted PR from 2004 to 2012; 194 applications rejected. Ceased 15 Apr 2012. Investment terms not found in official sources read (an MP said in 2012 that MAS had withdrawn it). Launch year taken from the period in the parliamentary answer ('From 2004 to 2012'), not confirmed.

new_indicators.name: Jobs created by programme investors
new_indicators.definition: Jobs reported as created in the host country by businesses of investors admitted through a residence- or citizenship-by-investment programme, cumulative over the stated period, as defined by the source
new_indicators.notes: Usually self-reported by investors and checked by the agency; say in notes whether limited to citizens.

new_indicators.name: Total business expenditure by programme investors
new_indicators.definition: Total business expenditure (operating plus capital spending) in the host country by companies of programme investors over the stated period, as reported by the programme agency. Not the same as the qualifying investment.
new_indicators.notes: Singapore GIP reports this for the direct-investment route.

new_indicators.name: Investor residence status retained
new_indicators.definition: Share of people granted residence through an investor programme in a period who still held that status on a later stated date

new_indicators.name: Investor residence renewals refused
new_indicators.definition: Programme residents whose residence permit, or re-entry permit tied to permanent residence, was not renewed because programme conditions were not met, in the stated period

new_indicators.name: Single family offices with tax incentives
new_indicators.definition: Number of single family offices (or their fund vehicles) holding a government tax incentive for family offices on a date, e.g. Singapore MAS sections 13O/13U
new_indicators.notes: Context for family-office residence routes; the incentive itself gives no residence right.

gaps: Annual GIP PR grants: only multi-year totals are published (2004-Jun 2017: 1,826; 2020-2022: ~200; 2015-2025: ~450). No year-by-year series, no applications received or rejected, no nationality breakdown, no count of dependants found.
The 2008-2010 figure ('close to 1,000 investors') and 2015-2025 figure (~450) cannot be reconciled with 1,826 to mid-2017 without annual data; 2017-2019 is missing.

Pre-2009 terms: the investment amounts in force from 2004 (and the scheme's pre-2004 history implied by the 1996 property rule) were not found in official documents; start dates of the S$1m/S$1.5m options are unknown.
No official document from March 2020 describing the revision (Option C) was found; terms are taken from the Aug 2021 factsheet.
Dates when the application fee changed (S$5,650 in 2012, S$7,000 in 2014, S$10,000 by 2021, S$20,000 by May 2025) were not found.
Financial Investor Scheme: investment terms, administering agency and legal basis not found in official sources.

Money-laundering case: no official source found that says whether any accused or associate held PR through the GIP. Official statements tie the case to Employment/Dependant's Passes and to tax-incentivised single family offices, not to the GIP. The SPF release mentions passports of foreign citizenship-by-investment countries; it says 'Dominican Republic', which some media later reported as Dominica - not checked.

No figure for total money committed through the GIP since 2004; investment figures cover different periods and routes (S$1.5bn 2008-2010; S$1.62bn in GIP funds to Oct 2022; S$500m direct + S$430m funds 2015-2025).
The Hansard search API returns loose matches; Chinese-language sources were not searched.
